headline: A 16-year-old hiker was rescued by helicopter from the foot of a cliff near Vancouver after following a route he had planned with AI.
score_reason: Pool score 2 lowered by 1: the rescue happened over the weekend, before the window, and the AI's role rests on the rescue team's account.
importance_line: Hikers who plan routes with an AI chatbot are the ones at risk, since the rescue team said a fall could have meant serious injury or death; the AI's role rests on the rescue team's account, and neither report shows the conversation itself.
summary: CTV News reports, citing North Shore Rescue search manager Paul Markey, that a 16-year-old hiker had to be rescued by a helicopter crew from the foot of a steep cliff on Crown Mountain near Vancouver over the weekend, after route instructions from the AI chatbot Claude, made by Anthropic, led him off the trail. Markey urged hikers not to follow AI directions blindly; an earlier Gizmodo report, citing North Shore News, said it was unclear which AI tool the teenager used, and the rescue team's own post said it was unclear exactly how he left the route.
notes: Pool item was Gizmodo, which relays North Shore News (original not found); credited CTV News, which interviewed the rescue team itself. Outlets differ on the day (Saturday per Gizmodo, Sunday per CTV) and on the AI tool (unclear per Gizmodo, Claude per CTV). Rescue was before the window, so follow-up of 4 Oct 2026 and score lowered by 1. The chatbot named is Claude, the writer's own model family; wording kept strictly to the reports.
